Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def comps(g):
    seen=set(); res=[]

                col=g[i][j]; q=deque([(i,j)]); seen.add((i,j)); cells=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cells.append((a,b))
                    for da in(-1,0,1):
                        for db in(-1,0,1):
                            x,y=a+da,b+db
                            if 0<=x<len(g) and 0<=y<len(g[0]) and g[x][y]==col and (x,y) not in seen:
                                seen.add((x,y)); q.append((x,y))
                res.append((col,cells))
    return res

    W=len(I[0]); out=[[0]*W for _ in range(9)]
    for a,b in kept[1]: out[a-6][b]=kept[0]
    kcol=min(a for a,_ in kept[1])-6
    # recompute kept rows after shift
    kr=[a-6 for a,_ in kept[1]]; kc=[b for _,b in kept[1]]
    k0=min(kc); k1=max(kc)
    kt=min(kr)
    for other in others:
        ocells=other[1]; oc=other[0]
        o0=min(b for a,b in ocells); o1=max(b for a,b in ocells)

        if try_place(kt-1):

    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])

    objs=[]
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            if inp[i][j]!=5 and not seen[i][j]:
                c=inp[i][j]; q=deque([(i,j)]); seen[i][j]=True; cs_=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cs_.append((a,b))
                    for da in(-1,0,1):
                        for db in(-1,0,1):
                            x,y=a+da,b+db
                            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and not seen[x][y] and inp[x][y]==c:
                                seen[x][y]=True; q.append((x,y))
                r0=min(a for a,b in cs_); r1=max(a for a,b in cs_)
                c0=min(b for a,b in cs_); c1=max(b for a,b in cs_)
                objs.append([c,r0,r1,c0,c1,cs_])
    bottom=[o for o in objs if o[1]>5]
    ones=[o for o in bottom if o[0]==1]
    kept=ones[0]; kcells=kept[5]; kr0,kr1=kept[1],kept[2]; kc0,kc1=kept[3],kept[4]
    others=[o for o in objs if o[1]<5 and o not in bottom and o[0]!=2]

    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]

    # other: aligned columns to kept piece span, flush adjacent vertically; side chosen by fit
    sides=[]

    base=None
    if len(sides)==1: base=sides[0][1]

        # choose side whose placement keeps other piece fully inside canvas AND prefer side matching original relative order (above if other originally above kept)
        orig_above = or1 < kr0   # roughly
        if orig_above: base=sides[0][1]

    else: base=sides[0][1]
    bc0=kc0
    for r,c in ocells:

    return out

def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    seen=[[False]*w for _ in range(h)]; objs=[]
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            if inp[i][j]!=5 and not seen[i][j]:
                c=inp[i][j]; q=deque([(i,j)]); seen[i][j]=True; cs_=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cs_.append((a,b))
                    for da in(-1,0,1):
                        for db in(-1,0,1):
                            x,y=a+da,b+db
                            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and not seen[x][y] and inp[x][y]==c:
                                seen[x][y]=True; q.append((x,y))
                r0=min(a for a,b in cs_); r1=max(a for a,b in cs_)
                c0=min(b for a,b in cs_); c1=max(b for a,b in cs_)
                objs.append([c,r0,r1,c0,c1,cs_])
    bottom=[o for o in objs if o[1]>5]
    ones=[o for o in bottom if o[0]==1]
    kept=ones[0]; kcells=kept[5]; kr0,kr1=kept[1],kept[2]; kc0,kc1=kept[3],kept[4]

    bc0=kc0

def pieces_of(g, skip=None):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    seen=[[False]*w for _ in range(h)]; res=[]
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            if g[i][j]!=5 and not seen[i][j]:
                c=g[i][j]; q=deque([(i,j)]); seen[i][j]=True; cs_=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cs_.append((a,b))
                    for da in(-1,0,1):
                        for db in(-1,0,1):
                            x,y=a+da,b+db
                            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and not seen[x][y] and g[x][y]==c:
                                seen[x][y]=True; q.append((x,y))
                r0=min(a for a,b in cs_); r1=max(a for a,b in cs_)
                c0=min(b for a,b in cs_); c1=max(b for a,b in cs_)
                res.append({'c':c,'r0':r0,'r1':r1,'c0':c0,'c1':c1,'cells':cs_})
    return res

    cfg=pieces_of(inp)

    # general: 1-pieces anywhere; the kept one chosen by cost minimization among (1-piece + non-2 pieces) permutations
    non2=[p for p in cfg if p['c']!=2]
    best=None
    for kept in [p for p in non2 if p['c']==1]:
        others=[p for p in non2 if p is not kept]
        others.sort(key=lambda p:p['r0'])
        kr0=kept['r0']; kcr=kept['c0']; kcl=kept['c1']
        # assign: place pieces adjacent vertically preserving order; above if possible else below
        above_span=kr0-1; below_span=h-1-(kr0-6)  # kept occupies rows kr0-6..kr0-3
        # greedily pack

        stack=[]
        cur_r=above_span  # topmost free row adjacent above kept
        below_rows=list(range(kr0-5,h))  # rows below kept final (kr0-6+1..h-1)
        idx=0
        for o in others:
            hh=o['r1']-o['r0']+1
            if idx<len(others) and cur_r>=0 and len(stack)+hh<=above_span+1:
                stack.append((cur_r,o))
                cur_r-=hh
            else:
                bb=below_rows[:hh]
                if len(bb)==hh:
                    stack.append((bb[0],o)); below_rows=below_rows[hh:]
                else:
                    pass  # conflict -> penalize heavily
        # cost = movement sum + conflict penalty
        tot=0; conf=0

        if conf: tot+=999
        cand=(tot,conf,kept)

        if cur>=0:
            for r,c in o['cells']: out[cur+r-o['r0']][kc0+(c-o['c0'])]=o['c']
            cur-=hh
        else:
            base=kept['r0']-5+1
            for r,c in o['cells']: out[base+r-o['r0']][kc0+(c-o['c0'])]=o['c']
    return out

def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    cands=comps(inp)
    anchors=[p for p in cands if p[0]==1 and max(a for a,_ in p[1])>5]
    anchor=max(anchors,key=lambda p:max(a for a,_ in p[1]))
    acells=anchor[1]; ar0=min(a for a,_ in acells); akc0=min(b for _,b in acells)
    kcs=[(a-ar0,b-akc0) for a,b in acells]
    others=[p for p in cands if p[0]!=2 and p not in [anchor]]
    mover=max(others,key=lambda p:max(b for _,b in p[1]))
    bcells=mover[1]; br0=min(a for a,_ in bcells); bc0=min(b for _,b in bcells)
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    # shift anchor up 6; also check: is output position actually rows (ar0-6..)? just place at -6 relative to original rows
    for a,b in acells: out[a-6][b]=1
    below_base=(ar0-6)+1 if ar0-6+1<h else None
    above_base=(ar0-6)-1 if ar0-6-1>=0 else None
    bases=[x for x in (below_base,above_base) if x is not None]
    base=min(bases,key=lambda b:abs(br0-b))  # minimize movement of mover's top
    for r,c in sorted(bcells): out[base+r-br0][bc0+(c-bc0)]=mover[0]
    return out

    allok&=r==e
print('ALL', allok)

from collections import deque
def comps(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*w for _ in range(h)]; res=[]
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            if g[i][j]!=5 and not seen[i][j]:
                c=g[i][j]; q=deque([(i,j)]); seen[i][j]=True; cells=[]
                while q:
                    a,b=q.popleft(); cells.append((a,b))
                    for da in(-1,0,1):
                        for db in(-1,0,1):
                            x,y=a+da,b+db
                            if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and not seen[x][y] and g[x][y]==c:
                                seen[x][y]=True; q.append((x,y))
                res.append((c,cells))
    return res
def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    cs=comps(inp)
    # kept = color-1 piece with largest row (below divider)
    kept=max([p for p in cs if p[0]==1],key=lambda p:max(a for a,_ in p[1]))
    mover=[p for p in cs if p[0]!=2 and p[0]!=1 and len(p[1])>1]
    mover=mover[0]
    kcells=kept[1]; mcells=mover[1]
    kr0=min(a for a,_ in kcells); kc0=min(b for _,b in kcells)
    mr0=min(a for a,_ in mcells); mc0=min(b for _,b in mcells)
    kh=max(a for a,_ in kcells)-kr0+1; kw=max(b for _,b in kcells)-kc0+1
    mh=max(a for a,_ in mcells)-mr0+1; mw=max(b for _,b in mcells)-mc0+1
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(9)]
    for r,c in kcells: out[r-kr0-6][c-kc0+kc0]=1   # shift up 6
    # stack flush: mover above kept (its original side), align columns to kept span
    top=(kr0-6)-1
    for r,c in mcells:
        sc=kc0+( (c-mc0)*(kw-1)//(mw-1) ) if mw>1 else kc0
        out[top-r+mr0][sc]=mover[0]
    return out
ok=True
for n in range(1,5):
    r=f(G[f'Demo pair {n} input']); e=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    print(n, r==e)
    ok&=r==e
print('ALL',ok)
if ok: print(json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])))

def bb(cells): return (min(x[0] for x in cells),max(x[0] for x in cells),min(x[1] for x in cells),max(x[1] for x in cells))
def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    cs=comps(inp)
    d=[i for i in range(h) if all(x==5 for x in inp[i])][0]
    kept=[p for p in cs if p[0]==1 and min(x[0] for x in p[1])>d and len(p[1])>1][0]
    m=[p for p in cs if p[0] not in (0,1,2) and len(p[1])>1][0]
    kt=min(x[0] for x in kept[1]); kb=max(x[0] for x in kept[1])
    mt=min(x[0] for x in m[1]); mb=max(x[0] for x in m[1])
    base=kt-6
    side='above' if mt<d else 'below'
    mv=base-1 if side=='above' else base+1
    H=max(base+kb, mv+mb)+1
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(H)]
    for r,c in kept[1]: out[r-base][c]=inp[r][c]
    for r,c in m[1]: out[mv+r-mt][c]=inp[r][c]
    # horizontal alignment: move mover toward kept until flush/adjacent (no overlap)
    kbb=(min(x[1] for x in kept[1]),max(x[1] for x in kept[1]))
    mbb=bb(m[1])
    o=0
    while True:
        nml=mbb[2]-o; nmr=mbb[3]-o
        if nml<=kbb[0] and nmr>=kbb[1]: break   # overlaps column span -> stop before it would cross
        if nmr<kbb[0]+1 or nml>kbb[1]-1: break  # gap >=2 -> continue sliding toward kept
        o+=1 if nml>kbb[1]-1 else -1
    for r,c in m[1]: out[mv+r-mt][c-o]=inp[r][c]
    return out
for n in range(1,5):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    print(n, f(gi)==go)

    mt=min(x[0] for x in m[1]); mb=max(x[0] for x in m[1])
    base=kt-6

In demo 3 output: pieces at rows 1-3 (kept shape moved? no—output shows a piece at rows 1-3 cols 6-8 which is the KEPT square's shape, and mover rows 4-6). Actually output keeps both copies! Wait demo 1 output: row2-4 mover (3-piece), rows 5-7 kept square. The ORIGINAL top copy of the hollow square is gone; the bottom one moved up to row 5 (shifted up 6 from 11). So output = moved kept square + mover, side-by-side vertically stacked, aligned how?

Demo 1: kept square at rows 5-7 cols 5-7; mover rows 2-4 cols 5-7. Same columns! So rule: keep the bottom hollow-square copy, shift it up so its bottom touches the divider+... no wait, it stops 1 row below where it was relative to the other copy? Originally there were two copies: top at rows 1-3, bottom at rows 11-13. Output puts them flush together at rows 2-7 (8 rows total, 1 empty row above?). Output height 9 (rows 0-8): rows 2-4 mover, 5-7 kept. Hmm why rows 2-4 not 1-3 or 3-5?

Demo 3: output rows 1-3 piece (cols 6-8, that's the kept shape — actually kept square shape rows 1-3 = original position of top copy!), and mover rows 4-6 cols 6-8. So in demo 3, the OUTPUT positions the kept copy AT THE TOP COPY'S ORIGINAL POSITION (rows 1-3), and the mover below it rows 4-6. Interesting — so instead of shifting by 6, the kept piece goes to where the other copy was (flush adjacent, occupying that space), and the mover takes the next 3 rows below? But demo 1: top copy was rows 1-3 cols 2-4, but output has nothing at rows 1-3 cols 2-4 except background — instead kept at rows 5-7 cols 5-7. Hmm inconsistent unless column alignment matters: kept stays in its own columns, moves to be flush with divider distance preserved?

Check demo 1: kept originally rows 11-13. Divider at row 5. Moved to rows 5-7: exactly touching divider (bottom at 7, divider top at 5, gap of row 4? No: kept occupies 5-7, divider row 5?? wait divider is row 5 in input. Output: row 4 is background, kept at 5-7. So kept moved to start right after divider. Demo 3: kept originally rows 7-9 (below divider row 5). Output kept at rows 1-3 — that's NOT after divider. Hmm.

Alternative interpretation: the two hollow square copies MERGE: they move to the same location, stacked flush. Total height 3+3=6 rows placed somewhere. Output total content rows 2-8 in demo1 (7 rows: 3+3 overlap? no). Demo1 output: rows 2-7, two pieces stacked vertically flush: mover rows 2-4, kept rows 5-7. Together 6 rows at rows 2-7. Where placed? Topmost at row 2. Why 2? Original: top copy at rows 1-3, bottom at 11-13. Distance between them: 8 rows (1→11). If they merge flush and are centered? Rows 2-7 centered around... hmm output grid height 9.

Maybe: the two copies slide toward each other until flush, then continue until they touch something? Or: kept copy moves up until it touches the divider OR reaches the other copy. In demo 3: kept rows 7-9, top copy rows 1-3 (cols 2-4 vs kept cols 6-8 — different columns!). In demo 3 output: kept shape at rows 1-3 cols 6-8?? Let me recheck: demo 3 go bboxes: (1,1,3,6,8,5) color 1 at rows 1-3 cols 6-8 — same COLUMNS as original kept (cols 6-8)! And mover rows 4-6 cols 6-8. So kept stays in its own columns, moves UP to align flush with the other copy's position range (top copy was rows 1-3 cols 2-4; kept cols 6-8 don't match though). Kept ends at rows 1-3: its BOTTOM at 3, one row below divider? No divider row 5.

Hmm demo 3: kept at rows 1-3, which is exactly where the OTHER copy used to be (rows 1-3), just in its own columns. Demo 1: other copy was rows 1-3 cols 2-4; kept would go rows 1-3 cols 5-7 — but output has kept at rows 5-7. Doesn't match. Unless... in demo 1, kept moved to rows 5-7 because... let me recount demo1 output rows: rows 2-4 = 3, rows 5-7 = 3, row 8 blank. Total 9 rows but content rows 2-7.

Distance preservation? In demo 1: top copy rows 1-3, bottom rows 11-13: gap between them = rows 4,5,6,7,8,9,10 minus... they're 8 apart. After: mover 2-4, kept 5-7, gap 0. Demo 3: top rows 1-3, bottom rows 7-9, gap rows 4,5,6 = 3. After: contiguous 2-6... wait kept at 1-3? That's overlapping the other copy's rows. Confusing.

New idea: the pieces move toward each other along their rows: bottom piece moves up until it becomes flush with the top piece (which also moves down? no—top stays?). Demo3: top copy rows 1-3 stays; bottom (rows 7-9) moves up until flush: rows 4-6 → but output shows kept at rows 1-3! Opposite: bottom piece jumped to the top's place?! And mover filled rows 4-6.

Actually maybe: bottom hollow square moves to the top hollow square's location (same rows, same columns?), i.e., both copies collapse into the top location, and the mover fills in between. Demo 1: top copy rows 1-3; kept should then be rows 1-3 — but it's at 5-7. Doesn't fit unless... demo 1's "mover" 3-piece got priority: mover first moves, then? In demo 1 output order top-down: mover (rows2-4), kept (5-7). In demo 3: kept rows 1-3, mover rows 4-6. So in demo1 the stack is Mover-over-Kept, demo3 Kept-over-Mover. What differs? Their original relative positions: demo1 mover (color 3) was ABOVE divider? Demo1: color 3 piece rows 1-3 — above divider. Kept rows 11-13 below. Demo3: mover color 6 rows 1-3 above; kept rows 7-9 below. Both same configuration, yet different stacking order?!

Difference: demo1 kept moved to ROWS 5-7 (after divider), demo3 kept moved to rows 1-3 (above divider, overlapping original top copy). Hmm demo3: is the kept at rows 1-3 really color 1? bbox (1,1,3,6,8,5) yes. But wait maybe those are actually the MOVER in some rotated form? No, mover is 7 cells; kept is 8 cells... size check: demo3 output size 5 for that piece, moved pieces... The 3-cell count: kept had 8 cells, mover 7. Output piece sizes: (3,2,4,5,7) → 5 cells color 3 at rows 2-4 cols 5-7, and (1,1,3,6,8,5) 5 cells at rows 1-3. So output has TWO 5-cell pieces?? Input had a 5-cell color-1 piece at rows 1-3 cols 2-4 AND the bottom 1-piece 8 cells... wait demo3 input kept is (1,7,9,6,8,5) = 5 cells at rows 7-9! Let me recheck earlier: comps listed kept as (1,7,9,6,8,5)? Output: kept shape rows 1-3 cols 6-8, mover rows 4-6.

So rule candidate: the bottom hollow piece moves up to the top hollow piece's ROW span (rows 1-3), keeping its own columns (cols 6-8), and the mover stacks flush below it (rows 4-6), taking the columns... mover cols 6-8 too? Output mover cols 6-8: norm of that piece: rows4-6 cols6-8 shape ((0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2)) — same norm as input mover? Input mover norm demo3: ((0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2)) yes identical.

So in demo3: bottom copy → top copy's row band (flush above where mover will be? or just occupies the vacated band); mover → directly below, columns set so it's flush/aligned somehow. Mover cols 6-8 = kept cols. 

Demo1: bottom copy rows 11-13 → rows ? Output kept rows 5-7, mover rows 2-4. Top copy was rows 1-3. If bottom copy went to rows 1-3 (as in demo3), output would show color-1 at rows 1-3 — it doesn't. Instead moved to 5-7, and mover at 2-4 above it.

Hmm. What if instead: the whole assembly shifts so that... let me compute per demo the placement of the merged 6-row block:
- Demo1: rows 2-7 (mover 2-4, kept 5-7). Block starts at row 2.
- Demo2: go bboxes: (4,0,2,5,7,7) color 4 rows 0-2 cols 5-7; (1,3,5,5,7,5) color1 rows 3-5. Block rows 0-5.
- Demo3: block rows 1-6.
- Demo4: (1,3,5,8,10,5) rows 3-5; (7,6,8,8,10,4) rows 6-8. Block rows 3-8.

Maybe the block is positioned such that the TOP copy's original position... Demo2 top copy rows 1-3 cols 2-4; block rows 0-5. Hmm.

Maybe: pieces move toward each other until they collide — bottom moves up, top stays, and where they meet... they'd overlap. Alternatively pieces move apart?? Demo1: top rows 1-3, bottom 11-13 → final 2-7 (moved closer by 4 each?). Gaps: originally gap rows 4-10 (7 rows). Final adjacent (gap 0). Shift amounts: top moved down 1 (1→2), bottom up 4 (11→7)? or top stayed 1-3ish? top was rows1-3, final top of block row 2: top moved down 1. Bottom rows 11-13 → 5-7: moved up 4. Total closure 5 rows but gap was 7... they met leaving 1 empty row (row 0-1?) — final rows 2-7, rows 0,1 empty. Gap closed by 5 of 7.

Demo3: top rows 1-3 stays, bottom 7-9 → 4-6 (up 3). Gap originally rows 4-6 (3). Closed fully, meeting in middle. Demo4: top rows 1-3, bottom 9-11 → 6-8 (down 3? bottom moved up 3), top down 2 (1→3). Gap rows 4-8 (5). They passed through each other's rows? Top rows 1-3 → 3-5, bottom 9-11 → 6-8, meeting at gap row... rows 3-8 consecutive. Closed fully, no overlap.

Demo2: top rows 1-3 → 0-2 (up 1), bottom 9-11 → 3-5 (down 6). Consecutive 0-5.

So pattern: pieces move toward each other and become adjacent (consecutive rows), preserving which piece is above/below (stacking order unchanged!). Now horizontal: movers end at kept's columns (demo1: cols 5-7 both; demo3: cols 6-8 both; demo2: kept cols 5-7, mover cols 5-7 ✓; demo4: kept cols 8-10, mover cols 8-10 ✓). And kept keeps its columns. So mover slides horizontally to align columns with kept (specifically align bounding box left edges? all cases mover cols == kept cols exactly).

Vertical placement within the adjacent pair: who ends on top? Preserved original order (above-stays-above). Row positioning: pair becomes consecutive rows, placed where? Demo1: pair rows 2-7; original top row 1, bottom row 11. Midpoint ~6; pair center = (2+7)/2=4.5; originally center 6. Not preserved. Demo2: pair 0-5 center 2.5; orig centers: top 2, bottom 10. Demo3: pair 1-6 center 3.5; orig centers top 2, bottom 8. Demo4: pair 3-8 center 5.5; orig centers top 2, bottom 10.

What determines absolute position? Perhaps the pair aligns so the TOP piece's position is preserved... demo3 top rows 1-3 → final kept rows 1-3! Yes! Wait demo1 final: mover rows 2-4, kept rows 5-7. Top copy was rows 1-3 cols 2-4. If top stayed, kept would be at rows 1-3 — it isn't.

Alternative: the PAIR is placed adjacent such that... the TOTAL vertical span equals original span? Demo1: original span rows 1-13 (13 rows); final rows 2-7 (6). Nope.

Maybe the pair position preserves the position of the TOP piece when possible without overlap: demo3: top rows 1-3, bottom could go to 4-6 fine → bottom moves to 4-6 ✓, top stays. Demo4: top rows 1-3, bottom rows 9-11; moving bottom up until adjacent means rows 4-6 — but final bottom is 6-8, top is 3-5!! Top moved DOWN to 3-5. Contradiction with "top stays".

Unless in demo4 the roles differ: maybe pieces can't overlap columns... they don't here. Hmm, demo4: what if the bottom piece (or whichever is farther) moves, and the constraint is the piece does NOT cross the divider row region?? Divider at row 5. Constraint hypothesis: the kept piece moves up so that its top... no wait, in demo4 kept ended at 3-5 including row 5 = divider. Hmm that breaks it, unless the divider counts as erasable and the piece overlaps it? Then adjacency: kept rows 3-5, mover 6-8, divider at 5 removed, so pieces ARE adjacent (rows 3-5 and 6-8 touch via row 5 boundary). OK so constraint might just be: pieces become adjacent (no gap), stacking order preserved, and maybe the piece that "moves" is chosen so they don't pass each other... but demo4 top moved down.

Simplest consistent rule: final pair is consecutive rows; preserve order; place the PAIR so that... the original relative ordering of rows is preserved globally? I.e., each piece keeps its row ORDER: the top piece's rows map to the lower rows of the pair, bottom to upper? Demo1: top→rows 2-4 (upper), bottom→5-7 (lower): order preserved, top on top ✓. Demo4: top→3-5 upper, bottom→6-8 lower ✓. Demo3: top→1-3 upper ✓. Demo2: top→0-2 ✓. Always top stays on top, adjacent, and the pair's position: needs a rule. Pair spans: demo1 rows 2-7, demo2 0-5, demo3 1-6, demo4 3-8. Original top rows, bottom rows: d1: top 1, bot 11; d2: top 1, bot 9; d3: top 1, bot 7; d4: top 1, bot 9. Pair tops: 2,0,1,3. Pair bottoms: 7,5,6,8.

Maybe the pair is centered on the original midpoint? Midpoints: d1 (1+11)/2=6 → pair center 4.5. d2 (1+9)/2=5 → center 2.5. d3 (1+7)/2=4 → 3.5. d4 (1+9)/2=5 → 5.5. Centers decrease by ~0.5 each time... pattern: 4.5,2.5,3.5,5.5. Alternating +/-2? d1:+2, d2:-2.5, d3:-0.5, d4:+0.5. Meh.

Alternatively pair is placed to maximize contact with... the DIVIDER? d1: pair 2-7, divider at 5 → divider inside pair. d2: divider row 5, pair 0-5 → divider at bottom edge. d3: divider 5, pair 1-6 → inside. d4: divider 5, pair 3-8 → inside. Hmm d2 unique.

Maybe pair placed adjacent to divider? d2: pair ends at row 5 = divider row — divider erased anyway. d1 pair contains divider row 5. All contain or touch.

Try another angle: perhaps each piece individually translates by a fixed amount related to its own geometry, like "move each piece 6 rows"? Kept demo1: 11-13 → 5-7 (−6). Demo2: 9-11 → 3-5 (−6). Demo3: 7-9 → 1-3 (−6). Demo4: 9-11 → 3-5 (−6). YES! Kept always moves up exactly 6 rows (verified earlier). Mover: demo1: 1-3 → 2-4 (+1). Demo2: 1-3 → 0-2 (−1). Demo3: 1-3 → 4-6 (+3). Demo4: 1-3 → 6-8 (+5).

Mover displacement = 1 − kept displacement (to close the gap / make adjacent with order preserved): d1: 1 − 6 = −5 → new top = 1−5=... wait mover top new = old top + disp. d1: mover +1? old 1 → new 2: +1. kept −6. Sum of changes = −5, closing gap of 7 (rows 4..10 minus overlap...). d2: mover −1, kept −6, sum −7, gap originally rows 5-8 (4 rows) plus divider... original gap between mover bottom (3) and kept top (9): rows 4-8 (5 rows incl divider at 5). Final adjacent: gap closed entirely (moved −7 total). d1 gap between mover bottom 3 and kept top 11: rows 4-10 (7 rows). Moved −5 total → adjacent ✓. d3: gap rows 4-6 (3), moved −3 ✓. d4: gap rows 4-8 (5), moved −5 ✓. Consistent: movers and kept approach each other until adjacent, kept moving 6 rows, mover moving the rest. Sign convention: both move toward each other.

Now horizontal: mover aligns columns with kept: d1 mover 10-12 → 5-7 (shift −5); kept cols 5-7. d2: mover 6-8 → 5-7 (−1). d3: mover 10-12 → 6-8 (−4). d4: mover 9-11 → 8-10 (−1). All: mover left col = kept left col. Simple: align left edges. Good.

Test input: kept = color 1 piece BELOW divider: rows 11-13 cols 1-3 (shape norm from bboxes: (1,11,13,1,3,5)). Mover: color 8, rows 1-3 cols 10-12 (5 cells). Also color 2 piece rows 1-3 cols 6-8 (5 cells) — noise, ignore. Kept moves up 6: rows 5-7 cols 1-3. Mover aligns left col to 1: cols 1-3. Vertical: moved to make adjacent, order preserved (mover originally above → above). Kept new top 5 → mover bottom = 4, mover top = 2. Disp for kept −6, so mover +? gap between mover bottom (3) and kept new top (5) = 1 row (row 4). Need mover to fill rows 2-4: new top = 2 = old top 1 + 1. So mover moves +1 (down 1).

Output grid: rows 0-? Height = max(5+kb, 4+mb)+1 = max(8,6)+1=9 rows. Columns 15.
Rows 2-4: mover shape: cells rel: (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(2,1),(2,2) at cols 1-3:
row2: (2,1)
row3: (3,1),(3,2)

row7: (7,1)

Build and validate against all demos with this full rule.

def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    cs=comps(inp)
    d=[i for i in range(h) if all(x==5 for x in inp[i])][0]
    kept=[p for p in cs if p[0]==1 and min(x[0] for x in p[1])>d and len(p[1])>1][0]
    m=[p for p in cs if p[0] not in (0,1,2) and len(p[1])>1][0]
    kcol=min(x[1] for x in kept[1]); ke=max(x[1] for x in kept[1])
    mt=min(x[0] for x in m[1]); mb=max(x[0] for x in m[1])
    mc=min(x[1] for x in m[1]); mr=max(x[1] for x in m[1])
    kt=min(x[0] for x in kept[1]); kb=max(x[0] for x in kept[1])
    base=kt-6           # kept moves up exactly 6
    mv_top = base-1      # mover stacks flush above kept
    H=mv_top+(mb-mt)+1  # height = mover extent +1
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(H)]
    for r,c in kept[1]: out[r-base][c]=inp[r][c]
    for r,c in m[1]: out[mt+r-(mt)-0 if False else 0][c-(mc-kcol)]=inp[r][c]  # placeholder
    return out

def f(inp):
    h,w=len(inp),len(inp[0])
    cs=comps(inp)
    d=[i for i in range(h) if all(x==5 for x in inp[i])][0]
    kept=[p for p in cs if p[0]==1 and min(x[0] for x in p[1])>d and len(p[1])>1][0]
    m=[p for p in cs if p[0] not in (0,1,2) and len(p[1])>1][0]
    kcol=min(x[1] for x in kept[1]); ke=max(x[1] for x in kept[1])
    mt=min(x[0] for x in m[1]); mb=max(x[0] for x in m[1])
    mc=min(x[1] for x in m[1]); mr=max(x[1] for x in m[1])
    kt=min(x[0] for x in kept[1]); kb=max(x[0] for x in kept[1])
    base=kt-6
    mv_top=base-1
    off=kcol-mc
    H=mv_top+mb-mt+1
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(H)]
    for r,c in kept[1]: out[r-base][c]=inp[r][c]
    for r,c in m[1]: out[mv_top+r-mt][c-off]=inp[r][c]
    return out

    print(n, r==go)
    if r!=go:
        for i in range(len(go)):

def pieces_of(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    cs=comps(g)
    res=[]
    for p in cs:
        if len(p[1])==1: continue
        cells=[(r,c) for r,c in p[1]]
        cols={x[1] for x in cells}
        if len(cols)==1 or all(x[1]==min(cols) for x in cells): continue
        res.append((min(x[0] for x in cells), min(x[1] for x in cells), max(x[0] for x in cells), max(x[1] for x in cells), cells))
    return res
for n in range(1,5):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    pi=pieces_of(gi); po=pieces_of(go)
    print('pair',n,'in pcs:',pi)
    print('out pcs:',po)

    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    dr=[r for r in range(h) if any(x==5 for x in gi[r])]
    d=dr[0]
    comp=components(gi)
    # group comps: exclude those touching divider row d and color 2
    top=[]; bot=[]
    for c,cl in comp:

            pass
    # simply: comps with all rows < d are 'above'; comps with rows > d+1 'below' (divider may have other things)
    A=[];B=[]
    for c,cl in comp:
        if max(r for r,_ in cl)<d: A.append((c,cl))
        elif min(r for r,_ in cl)>d: B.append((c,cl))
    # A should contain one dup pair (same shape, different positions); B the unique
    assert len(A)==2, (A)
    cA,a=A[0]; cB,b=B[0]
    nA,oA=norm(a); nB,oB=norm(b)
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    # decide: stationary = piece above with... in demos A (top) stayed, B moved up
    # fill: stationary first
    for r,c in sorted(a): out[r][c]=cA
    # mover: shift up until flush against stationary's bottom

    sta_bot=max(r for r,_ in a); sta_top=min(r for r,_ in a)
    # try shifting B up by k so that B becomes adjacent (no gap, no overlap)
    for k in range(1,h):
        mr=min(r-k for r,_ in b)
        if mr == sta_bot+1:

        if mr<sta_bot-1: continue

    # erase original B location

import itertools
def components(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); seen=[[False]*w for _ in range(h)]; out=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if g[r][c]!=0 and not seen[r][c]:
                st=[(r,c)]; comp=set()
                while st:
                    rr,cc=st.pop()
                    if (rr,cc) in comp or g[rr][cc]==0 or seen[rr][cc]: continue
                    comp.add((rr,cc))
                    seen[rr][cc]=True
                    for dr in(-1,0,1):
                        for dc in(-1,0,1):
                            if (dr,dc)!=(0,0) and 0<=rr+dr<h and 0<=cc+dc<w and g[rr+dr][cc+dc]!=0 and not seen[rr+dr][cc+dc]:
                                st.append((rr+dr,cc+dc))
                out.append((g[r][c],sorted(comp)))
    return out
def bbox(cells):
    rs=[r for r,_ in cells]; cs=[c for _,c in cells]
    return min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)

    rs=[r for r,_ in cells]; cs=[c for _,c in cells]
    mr=min(rs); mc=min(cs)
    return tuple(sorted((r-mr,c-mc) for r,c in cells)),(mr,mc)

for n in range(1,5):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    d=max(r for r in range(len(gi)) if any(x==5 for x in gi[r]))
    comps=components(gi)
    A=[c for c,_ in comps if max(r for r,_ in [p for p in []]) ] if False else None
    above=[cl for c,cl in comps if c!=5 and all(r<d for r,_ in cl)]
    below=[cl for c,cl in comps if c!=5 and min(r for r,_ in cl)>d]
    bn=norm(below[0])[0]; dup=[cl for cl in above if norm(cl)[0]==bn][0]
    oth=[cl for cl in above if cl is not dup]
    H,W=len(go),len(go[0])
    got=set((r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if go[r][c])
    print('=== pair',n,'keptcols',sorted(set(x for row in go for x in row if x)),'dims',H,W)
    for name,cl in (('dup',dup),('other',oth[0])):
        s=sig(cl); print(name,'orig at',(s[1],s[2]),'sig_len',len(s[0]))
    # find translation of dup in output: colors by shape? use matching sig with color from go
    gc=components(go)
    print(' out comps sigs:',[(c,s) for c,s in [(cc,len(norm(sl)[0])) for cc,sl in gc]])

from collections import Counter
def solve(gi):
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    # divider: row separating two big background regions; find it as row r where background(0)-component splits
    bg=comps([row[:] for row in gi])  # comps includes everything incl color0
    # identify the two giant 0-regions: take largest two comps of color 0
    big=[p for p in comps(gi) if p[0]==0]
    big.sort(key=lambda p:-len(p[1]))
    cA,clA=big[0]; cB,clB=big[1]
    rsA={r for r,_ in clA}; rsB={r for r,_ in clB}
    d=min(max(rsA),max(rsB))-max(min(rsA),min(rsB))  # divider row index somewhere
    # divider is the row just between them: candidates rows between the regions
    cands=set(range(h)) - rsA - rsB
    # choose candidate row with most 5s or that separates
    dr=max(cands,key=lambda r: sum(1 for x in gi[r] if x==5) ) if any(x==5 for x in gi[cands]) else None
    # fallback: simply the row where neither big comp has cells
    d=max((r for r in cands if all(x!=0 or True for x in gi[r])), default=None)  # placeholder
    return d,big,dr,gi

def solve(gi):
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    d=min(r for r in range(h) if any(x==5 for x in gi[r]))
    pieces=[p for p in comps_of(gi) if p[0]!=5 and len(p[1])>=2]
    b=[x for x in pieces if min(r for r,_ in x[1])>d]; a=[x for x in pieces if min(r for r,_ in x[1])<d]
    dup=max(b,key=len)
    ds=norm(dup[1])
    others=[x for x in a if norm(x[1])!=ds]
    oth=None
    if others:
        oth=max(others,key=lambda x:max(c for _,c in x[1]))
    O=[[0]*w for _ in range(9)]
    dt=min(r for r,_ in dup[1]); dc=min(c for _,c in dup[1])
    for r,c in dup[1]: O[r-6][c]=dup[0]
    if oth:
        oh=max(r for r,_ in oth[1])-min(r for r,_ in oth[1])+1
        oc=min(c for _,c in oth[1]); ow=max(c for _,c in oth[1])
        dow=max(c for _,c in dup[1])
        # slide horizontally so other's column span = dup's span
        ocols=[(r, oc+dc-oc if False else dc-(oc-c)) for r,c in oth[1]]  # cols aligned to dup bbox [dc,dow]: target col range same as dup
        for r,c in ocols: pass
        # cells placed at col = c - (dc - oc) -> align left edges
        off=dc-oc
        best=None
        for top in (dt-oh, dt+1):
            if not all(0<=top+r<9 for r in range(oh)): continue
            cells={(top+r, c+off) for r,c in oth[1]}
            drows={(rt-6,cc) for rt,cc in dup[1]}
            if cells & drows: continue
            move=abs(top-min(r for r,_ in oth[1]))
            if best is None or move<best[0]: best=(move,top)
        _,top=best
        for r,c in oth[1]: O[top+r][c+off]=oth[0]
    return O
allok=True
for n in range(1,5):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    o=solve(gi); ok=o==go; allok&=ok
    print(n,ok)
print('ALL' if allok else 'NO')
if allok:
    import json
    ti=G['Test input']; res=solve(ti)
    print(json.dumps(res))

steps.input:
for n in range(1,5):
    gi=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; go=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    cs=comps_of(gi)
    d=min(r for r in range(len(gi)) if any(x==5 for x in gi[r]))
    kept=[p for p in cs if p[0]!=5 and len(p[1])>=2]
    print('== pair',n,'divider row',d)
    for col,cells in kept:
        r0=min(r for r,_ in cells); c0=min(c for _,c in cells)
        hh=max(r for r,_ in cells)-r0+1; ww=max(c for _,c in cells)-c0+1
        s=set(cells)
        print(' color',col,'top',r0,'left',c0,'size',len(cells),'bbox',hh,'x',ww)
        for rr in range(hh):
            print('   ',''.join('#' if (r0+rr,c0+cc) in s else '.' for cc in range(ww)))
    # output pieces
    oc=comps_of(go)
    print(' output pieces:')
    for col,cells in oc:
        print('  out color',col,'size',len(cells),'top',min(r for r,_ in cells),'left',min(c for _,c in cells))

    below=[p for p in cs if min(r for r,_ in p[1])>div]
    cluster=set().union(*[set(p[1]) for p in below])
    ocs=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]

    return None

def place(gi, cells, col, target_rows=None):
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    best=None
    for dr in range(-h,h):
        for dc in range(-w,w):
            mv={(r+dr,c+dc) for r,c in cells}
            if not (0<=min(r for r,_ in mv) and max(r for r,_ in mv)<h and 0<=min(c for _,c in mv) and max(c for _,c in mv)<=w-1): continue
            if mv & cluster: continue
            adj=any(abs(r-a)+abs(c-b)==1 for r,c in mv for a,b in cluster)
            dist=(abs(dr)+abs(dc))
            if adj and (best is None or dist<best[0]): best=(dist,(dr,dc),mv)
    return best

def solve2(gi):
    h,w=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    div=[r for r in range(h) if any(x==5 for x in gi[r])][0]
    cs=comps(gi)
    above=[p for p in cs if max(r for r,_ in p[1])<div]
    below=[p for p in cs if min(r for r,_ in p[1])>div]
    cluster=set().union(*[set(p[1]) for p in below])
    outg=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for p in below:
        for r,c in p[1]: outg[r][c]=p[0]
    for p in above:
        n=norm(*p)
        bc=next(q for q in below if norm(*q)==n)
        bs=bc[1]; bcol=bc[0]
        best=None
        for dr in range(-h,h):
            for dc in range(-w,w):
                mv={(r+dr,c+dc) for r,c in p[1]}
                if not (0<=min(r for r,_ in mv) and max(r for r,_ in mv)<h and 0<=min(c for _,c in mv) and max(c for _,c in mv)<=w-1): continue
                if mv & cluster: continue
                adj=any((a,b) in cluster for r,c in mv for a,b in [(r+1,c),(r-1,c),(r,c+1),(r,c-1)])
                if not adj: continue
                dist=sum(abs(dr)+abs(dc) for r,c in [(min(r for r,_ in p[1])+dr,min(c for _,c in p[1])+dc)])
                if best is None or dist<best[0]: best=(dist,(dr,dc))
        for r,c in p[1]: outg[r][c]=0
        if best:
            dr,dc=best
            for r,c in p[1]: outg[min(r for r,_ in p[1])+dr][min(c for _,c in p[1])+dc]=p[0]
        else:
            for r,c in p[1]: outg[min(r for r,_ in p[1])][min(c for _,c in p[1])]=p[0]
        cluster |= set(mv) if False else {(min(r for r,_ in p[1])+dr, min(c for _,c in p[1])+dc)} if False else set()
    return outg
